newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen extending light downtrend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen extending light downtrend.

text.p: Polish shares fell 0.6 percent after Wednesday's rise and analysts said mixed trade at order balancing and falls in continuous trade suggested the market would return to its slight downtrend on macroeconomic concerns.

"Generally the market is slipping the whole time, you can't see demand from foreign investors and you can see there are expectations of an interest-rate rise, especially as money supply is rising," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski of PBI brokerage.
Forex dealers on Thursday said immediate official rate rise expectations subsided but that the central bank might increase market rates quickly to cool fast growing domestic demand.
On Tuesday the statistics office announced that Polish broad money rose 2.8 percent in July's first 10 days.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.6 percent to 15,102.9 points and turnover rose 13.2 percent to 165.1 million zlotys ($47.8 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 67 to 19 with 20 stocks flat.

Analysts said macroeconomic concerns and the market mood were not helped by recent flooding in Poland which swamped more than one percent of the country and could lead to central bank lending to the government up to 2.5 billion zlotys ($723 million).
They said the run-up to parliamentary elections due on September 21 should also help continue the slight downtrend.
Analysts said garment maker Prochnik, down 9.8 percent, extended Wednesday's tumble on concerns its bourse price may have been manipulated with those of some parallel market firms.
On Tuesday the Securities Commission (KPW) said it had previously notified the public prosecutor that a group of investors may have illegally manipulated prices.
